newsitem.title: JAPAN: FUJITA SAYS AIMS TO CUT DEBT TO UNDER 400 BLN YEN.
newsitem.headline: FUJITA SAYS AIMS TO CUT DEBT TO UNDER 400 BLN YEN.

text.p: Fujita Corp said on Friday it aims to reduce its interest-bearing debt by 200 billion yen in the next five to six years to less than 400 billion yen in a bid to strengthen its financial status.
The Japanese construction firm had 637 billion yen worth of interest-bearing debt as of the end of March 1997.

Starting from the current business year, which ends on March 31, 1998, the company plans to repay 40 billion to 50 billion yen worth of debt per year, partly by selling some of its properties, a company spokesman said.

The company has previously told financial institutions with which it does business that it would reduce its interest-bearing debt by a total of 100 billion yen in the 1996/97 and 1997/98 business years.
Concurrently with the new debt-reduction plan, the company will also focus more on the profitability of construction projects with the aim of boosting profits, the spokesman said.
